name: Hierarchy View
tagline: A record's place in its hierarchy — ancestors above, children below — from its parent lookup.

limitations: The tree comes from the preset's Sample data, not from Dataverse. On a form the control reads the record's ancestors and children through context.webAPI — a FetchXML eq-or-above query on a hierarchical lookup, retrieveRecord and an OData $filter on one that is not — and there is no environment behind this origin to answer, so every preset carries a JSON tree in the sampleData property and the control renders that. Expanding a node and Show all children work against the same tree.

Which of the two routes a real form would take cannot be shown. The decision reads the relationship's IsHierarchical flag from EntityDefinitions, and the harness has no metadata to read; the presets carry childCount where a hierarchical lookup would supply it and omit it where the fallback route would not know.
Clicking a name opens nothing. The card calls navigation.openForm, and there is no form here to open — the harness reports the call and the tree stays.
The detail texts are the preset's own strings. On a form they are the platform's formatted values — a currency with its symbol, a choice as its label, a lookup as the related record's name.

Everything that never leaves the browser is real: the indented tree with its guide lines, the marked current record, chevrons and expansion, the show-all affordance on an ancestor, the narrow layout, dark, RTL, and the hidden and no-access states.

presets.name: A record in the middle
presets.description: Two ancestors above, two children below, a sibling waiting behind Show all children. The state most accounts are in.
